title: How to Close Credit Card in India 2026: Steps & Precautions
summary: How to close a credit card in India: steps for any bank, a ready application format, the RBI 7-day rule, and how to cancel without hurting your CIBIL score.
body_markdown:
Closing a credit card is easy. Closing it the right way, without hurting your CIBIL score or leaving loose ends, takes a little planning. This is a universal guide on **how to close a credit card** with any bank in India: what to finish before you apply, the exact steps to cancel, a ready application format, the RBI rule that protects you, and how to protect your credit score through the process.


## Closing a Credit Card at a Glance


**Who can close** The primary cardholder, for any bank's card


**Cost** Free. No bank can charge a closure fee


**Time limit** RBI rule: the bank must close it within 7 working days of a completed request


**Penalty on delay** Rs 500 per day of delay, payable by the bank to you


**Must be zero** Outstanding balance, pending EMIs, and unbilled spends


**Main risk** A temporary dip in your CIBIL score if closed carelessly


## Before You Close: Finish These 6 Things


1. **Redeem all reward points.** Points, cashback, and other[credit card benefits](https://gromo.in/blog/credit-card-benefits/) usually lapse the day the card closes. Convert them to vouchers, statement credit, or products first.
2. **Clear the full outstanding.** Not just the billed amount. Check unbilled transactions and any pending EMIs; a card cannot close with dues.
3. **Close or transfer EMIs.** Purchases converted to EMI must be foreclosed or fully paid. Ask the bank for the foreclosure amount.
4. **Move your autopays.** Shift OTT subscriptions, utility bills, and any standing instructions to another card or UPI, or they will bounce silently.
5. **Wait for one final statement.** Small charges like interest or annual fee sometimes land late. A surprise Rs 100 due after closure can become a negative mark.
6. **Download your statements.** Save the last 6-12 months of statements before you lose netbanking access to the card.


## How to Close a Credit Card: Step by Step


1. **Call customer care** on the number behind your card and request closure. The bank may offer you a fee waiver or upgrade to keep you; decline politely if you have decided.
2. **Put it in writing.** Email the bank's card service ID or use the app or netbanking closure option. Many banks now have a card closure request inside the app itself.
3. **Note the service request number.** This is your proof of the date, which matters for the RBI 7-day rule.
4. **Verify the closure.** The bank confirms by email or SMS. Ask for a No Objection Certificate (NOC) or closure confirmation letter for your records.
5. **Destroy the card.** Cut through the chip and magnetic strip once closure is confirmed.
6. **Check your CIBIL report after 30-45 days.** The card should show as closed with zero balance. If it still shows active, raise a dispute with the bureau and the bank.


## Application Format to Close a Credit Card


If your bank asks for a written request, this simple format works for any bank. Send it from your registered email:


> Subject: Request to Close Credit Card ending XXXX
>
>
> Dear Sir/Madam,
>
>
> I request you to permanently close my credit card ending XXXX, registered under mobile number XXXXXXXXXX. I have cleared the full outstanding balance and redeemed my reward points. Kindly confirm the closure in writing and issue a No Objection Certificate. Please also confirm that no charges remain on the card.
>
>
> Name: \[Your full name\]
> Registered mobile: \[Number\]
> Date: \[Date\]
>
>
> Thank you.


## The RBI Rule That Protects You


Under RBI's credit card rules, once you have cleared all dues and submitted a closure request, the bank must close the card within **7 working days** . If it delays beyond that, the bank is liable to pay you **Rs 500 per day** of delay until closure. Banks must also offer multiple closure channels like helpline, email, app, or website, and cannot force you to visit a branch or send a courier. If a bank drags its feet, quote this rule in writing, and escalate to the RBI Ombudsman (cms.rbi.org.in) if needed.


## Does Closing a Credit Card Affect Your CIBIL Score?


Yes, it can, in two ways. Understanding them is how you close smartly:


Effect What happens How much it matters


Credit utilization rises Closing a card removes its limit. Your same spending now uses a bigger share of your remaining total limit The biggest short-term effect. Keep utilization under 30%


Account age shortens Closing an old card can reduce the average age of your credit history over time Matters most if you close your oldest card


Credit mix changes If it was your only card, you lose your revolving credit line entirely Small effect, but real for thin credit files


## How to Close a Credit Card Without Hurting Your CIBIL Score


1. **Keep your oldest card alive.** Close newer cards first; the oldest card anchors your credit history age.
2. **Check your total utilization first.** If closing the card pushes your spending above 30% of your remaining limits, pay down balances or ask for a limit increase on another card before closing.
3. **Close one card at a time.** Space closures a few months apart instead of cancelling several cards together.
4. **Keep at least one card active** and use it lightly with full on-time payments, so your score keeps building (see[how to improve your credit score](https://gromo.in/blog/how-to-improve-credit-score-india-2026/) for the full playbook).
5. **Time it away from big loans.** Avoid closures in the 3-6 months before a home or car loan application, when a temporary dip hurts the most.


## Think Twice: Alternatives to Closing


- **Annual fee is the problem?** Ask the bank to convert the card to a lifetime free variant (see all[types of credit cards](https://gromo.in/blog/types-of-credit-cards/) ). Most banks have a downgrade option to a[lifetime free credit card](https://gromo.in/blog/lifetime-free-credit-card/) , and you keep your limit and history.
- **Overspending is the problem?** Lower the credit limit or lock the card in the app instead of closing it.
- **Unused card?** One small recurring payment with autopay keeps it alive and your utilization low at zero effort.


## FAQ: How to Close a Credit Card


**Can closing a credit card affect my CIBIL score?**


Yes, usually as a temporary dip. Closing a card removes its credit limit, so your spending uses a bigger share of your remaining limits, which raises your credit utilization. Closing an old card can also shorten your average credit history age over time. The account itself stays on your report as a closed account with its payment history intact for years.


**How do I close a credit card without hurting my CIBIL score?**


Five rules: keep your oldest card open and close newer ones first, make sure your spending stays under 30% of your remaining limits before closing, close one card at a time with gaps of a few months, keep at least one active card with on-time payments, and avoid closures in the 3-6 months before applying for a big loan. Follow these and any dip is small and short.


**How do I write an application to close my credit card?**


Keep it short: subject line with the card's last 4 digits, a clear request for permanent closure, confirmation that dues are cleared and points redeemed, and a request for written closure confirmation plus an NOC. Send it from your registered email. This guide includes a ready format you can copy.


**How many days does a bank take to close a credit card?**


By RBI rule, the bank must close your card within 7 working days once you have cleared dues and submitted the request. If it takes longer, the bank has to pay you Rs 500 for every day of delay. Keep your service request number as proof of the request date.


**Should I close my credit card or just stop using it?**


If the annual fee is the issue, downgrading to a lifetime free variant is usually smarter than closing: you keep your limit, history, and score intact. Stop-and-hold works too if the card is free, but banks may close cards unused for about a year, so keep one small autopay on it. Close it fully when the fee cannot be waived and the benefits are not worth it.


**What happens to my reward points and EMIs when I cancel my card?**


Reward points lapse on closure, so redeem everything first. Running EMIs must be foreclosed or paid in full before the bank will close the card; ask for the foreclosure amount. Also move every autopay and subscription to another payment method, or those payments will start failing.
